news.headline: A Baby Zebra Named Astra Is Born
news.body: The Oklahoma City Zoo welcomed a brand-new zebra foal on Monday! Her name is Astra, which means "star" in Greek, and she weighed 82 pounds when she was born. That's about as heavy as a big dog! All the zebras at the zoo get space-themed names. Astra is a Plains zebra, the smallest and most common kind of zebra. Plains zebras come from the grasslands of eastern and southern Africa, and zoos are helping them because they are losing some of their wild homes.

news.headline: Kids Dream Up the World's Biggest Hairdryer
news.body: More than 5,000 kids ages 4 to 11 sent in ideas for a record-breaking invention. The winners, two girls named Kiki and Thea, picked a giant hairdryer! Engineers from the YouTube channel Kids Invent Stuff built it in three weeks. It is 1.6 meters (about 5 feet 3 inches) tall, roughly as tall as a grown-up, and about eight times bigger than a normal hairdryer. It takes four people to move it. Guinness World Records made it official, and yes, it really dried someone's hair!

news.headline: New Blades Could Help Mars Helicopters Fly Farther
news.body: In 2021, a little helicopter named Ingenuity became the first aircraft to fly on another planet: Mars! Now NASA engineers are testing new helicopter blades that are thinner and sharper. Mars has very thin air, so flying there is tricky. Computer tests show the new blades could let a Mars helicopter fly about 11 miles in one trip, instead of less than half a mile like Ingenuity. The blades aren't ready for Mars yet, but they could help future helicopters explore much more of the Red Planet.

fun_fact: A zebra's stripes are like a fingerprint. No two zebras in the whole world have exactly the same stripe pattern! 🦓
